topics.title: Chip stocks pull markets lower
topics.summary: Global markets dipped as worries about the AI trade hit major chipmakers, while strong earnings from Goldman Sachs and UnitedHealth helped cushion Wall Street.
topics.discussionPrompt: When investors suddenly cool on AI stocks, who thinks it is healthy caution and who starts defending every gadget in the room?

topics.title: IMF lifts growth forecast, flags risks
topics.summary: The IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, but warned that debt, low oil buffers and AI-driven market swings could test economic resilience.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the forecast says things are growing but still fragile, who celebrates the good news and who reads every footnote twice?

topics.title: Rwanda lands future F1 race
topics.summary: Formula 1 announced a 10-year deal for Rwanda to host an African Grand Prix in the early 2030s, marking the sport's planned return to the continent.
topics.discussionPrompt: If F1 comes back to Africa after decades away, who talks engineering dreams and who immediately asks about traffic near the track?

topics.title: Mexico storms damage Pacific coast
topics.summary: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel battered Mexico's Pacific coast, damaging infrastructure, causing flash floods and prompting helicopter rescues in affected communities.
topics.discussionPrompt: When two storms hit the same coastline, who focuses on rescue logistics and who starts redesigning the emergency checklist?

topics.title: Iguazu Falls temporarily closes
topics.summary: Argentina temporarily closed Iguazu Falls after El Nino-linked rains sent water levels surging, turning a tourist landmark into a safety concern.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a famous waterfall gets too powerful for visitors, who is awed by nature and who quietly cancels the group selfie plan?

topics.title: Epic Games leans harder into AI
topics.summary: Epic Games confirmed a major shift toward AI across its tools and projects, with CEO Tim Sweeney saying game development is changing quickly.
topics.discussionPrompt: If game studios go all-in on AI tools, who sees creative shortcuts and who worries the weird human touches disappear?

topics.title: Retail brands report cyber incident
topics.summary: TFG London, owner of Hobbs and Phase Eight, apologized for disruption after identifying a cybersecurity incident, while H&M investigated a separate hacking claim.
topics.discussionPrompt: When stores announce a cyber incident, who checks their password habits and who mainly wonders if their order still ships?

topics.title: Nevada data centers stir debate
topics.summary: Plans for AI data centers on federal land are reshaping Nevada politics, with supporters citing jobs and critics raising questions about water, power and public land.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a giant data center promises jobs but needs lots of resources, who sees progress and who asks where the water comes from?

topics.title: Yemen oil facilities reportedly struck
topics.summary: A Houthi-backed broadcaster said Saudi-led coalition strikes hit oil facilities west of Yemen's capital, adding another flashpoint to the region's escalating conflict.
topics.discussionPrompt: When reports from a conflict zone arrive fast, who wants confirmed details first and who worries about fuel prices by dinner?

topics.title: Coastal erosion claims English homes
topics.summary: New figures reported by The Guardian found at least 183 homes in England have been demolished over 16 years after coastal erosion made them unsafe.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the coastline keeps moving closer, who argues for better defenses and who asks whether people should move earlier?
